value.desc: The bar you hold the world to is nothing next to the one you hold yourself to. Finishing something and feeling finished are two different days for you.
New people often think you're judging them. You usually are, but not the way they fear, and by the time they learn that, some have already kept their distance.
You see where things are heading long before anyone else will say it out loud. Being right early feels a lot like being alone.
Once you've decided what something is, it stays decided. The person who grew, the plan that improved, the second chance that was earned, they all arrive to a door already shut.
You reach an answer, then reopen it, then reopen it again. The decision everyone's waiting on is still on your desk, not because you can't decide, but because deciding never feels finished.
